analysis.title: Why rebalance into fixed income?
key_insights: UBS CIO rates fixed income as Attractive and advises investors to review bond allocations and consider adding exposure, citing elevated starting yields and diversification benefits.

Global yields remain high due to inflation worries, persistent fiscal concerns, and rising hyperscaler debt issuance. The 10-year UST yield is around 4.95%, below the multi-decade high set in early October.
The 10-year German Bund yield stood at 3.30% at the time of writing, so European yields are also elevated.

UBS favors intermediate average duration, generally maturities of about two to 10 years, and is more cautious on the longest-dated bonds given fiscal sustainability concerns and AI-related debt issuance.
Emerging market and high yield bonds are favored on a relative basis for extra income. EM sovereign yields are about 7.1%, EM corporate about 7%, and US high yield about 8.4%.
US Treasury yields fell last week as investors sought stability amid an equity sell-off. The 2-year yield dropped nearly 20bp, its best weekly performance since August 2025.

Elevated outright yields give a carry cushion against further volatility that was not available in 2022. Investors should focus less on calling the peak in yields and more on using current starting yields.
For low-rate economies like Switzerland, UBS sees merit in equity income approaches and select structured strategies. Income-focused investors may prefer shorter maturities to reduce duration risk.
